text: Choose location sufficient disk space. paths derived single root_dir: OpenAlex publishes snapshot natively Parquet, conversion step: download ready index. (Earlier releases package shipped snapshot_to_parquet() converted old .json.gz distribution; removed, path dead.) snapshot hosted Amazon S3 updated regularly. aws s3 sync resumes interrupted downloads fetches new changed files: Expected time: 2–12 hours depending connection. Tip: monitor progress another terminal: entity directory Parquet files, hive-partitioned update date: works corpus bulk — order 900 GB across ~2,000 files, roughly 500 million records. Two consequences worth knowing start: Column projection main cost lever. Works carry ~51 columns, many deeply nested; abstract alone 10 GB. lookup_by_id() get_citing() take columns, naming need changes runtimes order magnitude. Point DuckDB spill directory fast local disk. Spilling onto external volume corpus measured 10x slower onto internal SSD. builders default temp_dir tempdir() reason; override tempdir() small slow. fast ID-based lookups, build index dataset: creates <root_dir>/parquet/<dataset>_id_idx/ dataset — partitioned directory, single file, lookup opens blocks needs. index maps OpenAlex ID physical location (file row number) lookup_by_id() can retrieve records without scanning corpus. Two indexes optional needed citation graph: build_citation_index() expensive one — materialises roughly three billion edges — resumable: completed batches skipped re-run, interrupted build continues rather restarting.
code: <root_dir>/   parquet/                    # the snapshot, plus the indexes built over it   openalex-snapshot_metadata/ # reports, logs, schema caches aws s3 sync \   s3://openalex \   /Volumes/external-drive/openalex/parquet \   --no-sign-request watch -n 60 'du -sh /Volumes/external-drive/openalex/parquet/*' parquet/ ├── works/ │   └── updated_date=YYYY-MM-DD/ │       ├── part_0000.parquet │       └── ... ├── authors/ ├── institutions/ ├── sources/ ├── publishers/ ├── funders/ └── topics/ build_corpus_index(   root_dir  = "/Volumes/external-drive/openalex",   data_sets = NULL,   # NULL = all datasets   workers   = 8 ) # Who cites whom. This inverts `referenced_works`, and is what makes the # forward direction possible offline at all: `cited_by_api_url` is a URL. build_citation_index(   root_dir = "/Volumes/external-drive/openalex",   workers  = 8 )  # Only if you want to resolve DOIs without the API. build_doi_index(root_dir = "/Volumes/external-drive/openalex")

title: Working with the OpenAlex Bulk Snapshot
text: IDs can supplied short form ("W2741809807") long form ("https://openalex.org/W2741809807"); accepted normalised automatically. complex analytical queries, use DuckDB directly:
code: library(openalexSnapshot)  # Extract specific works — output written to a temp directory out_dir <- tempfile() lookup_by_id(   index_file = "/Volumes/external-drive/openalex/parquet/works_id_idx.parquet",   ids        = c("W2741809807", "W2100837269"),   output_dir = out_dir )  # Read the results library(arrow) works <- open_dataset(out_dir) |> collect() library(duckdb) library(DBI)  con <- dbConnect(duckdb())  # Register parquet files as a view dbExecute(   con,   "   CREATE VIEW works AS   SELECT * FROM parquet_scan('/Volumes/external-drive/openalex/parquet/works/*.parquet')   " )  # Run analytical queries result <- dbGetQuery(   con,   "   SELECT publication_year, COUNT(*) AS n_works   FROM works   WHERE publication_year >= 2020   GROUP BY publication_year   ORDER BY publication_year   " )  dbDisconnect(con)

title: Working with the OpenAlex Bulk Snapshot
text: OpenAlex releases new snapshots regularly. recommended update workflow:
code: # Show bucket info (size, file count) aws s3 ls s3://openalex/data/ --no-sign-request --recursive --summarize | tail -2 # 1. Archive the current snapshot with a datestamp mv /Volumes/external-drive/openalex/snapshot \    /Volumes/external-drive/openalex/snapshot-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)  # 2. Download the new snapshot aws s3 sync \   s3://openalex \   /Volumes/external-drive/openalex/snapshot \   --no-sign-request  # 3. Archive the current parquet directory mv /Volumes/external-drive/openalex/parquet \    /Volumes/external-drive/openalex/parquet-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)

title: openalexSnapshot -- OpenAlex Bulk Snapshot Tools
code: library(openalexSnapshot)  root <- "/Volumes/openalex"  # OpenAlex now publishes the snapshot natively in Parquet, so there is no # JSON conversion step.  # 1. Build the ID index (record lookup) build_corpus_index(   root_dir  = root,   data_sets = "works",   workers   = 4 )  # 2. Build the citation index (who cites whom). This inverts #    referenced_works, which is what makes the forward direction possible #    offline -- cited_by_api_url is a URL and cannot be used. build_citation_index(root_dir = root, workers = 4)  # 3. Look up records by OpenAlex ID. `columns` matters: works carry ~51 #    columns of nested structs and extracting all of them dominates the run. works <- lookup_by_id(   root_dir = root,   ids      = c("W2741809807", "W2100837269"),   columns  = c("id", "doi", "title", "publication_year") )  # 4. Walk the citation graph citing <- get_citing("W2741809807", root_dir = root)   # works citing it cited  <- get_cited("W2741809807",  root_dir = root)   # works it cites
